subject: Clarifying where inference runs and third-party handoffs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@pepperhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwo od.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - Pepper Health <legal@pepperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial question — where does inference actually execute?

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Quick Q as we're doing a short security review ahead of procurement: for requests sent to Redwood's hosted API, where is the inference executed (region(s) + cloud provider)? Do you ever route requests through third-party subprocessors (including observability or logging vendors) in other countries? Our legal team is specifically asking whether any processing or caching could put Pepper Health PII into jurisdictions outside the US or EU.

Also — what are your deletion/retention commitments for prompt + response data for hosted customers (and how that changes for Dedicated vs Private deployments)? Any standard timeframe and whether you support immediate deletion requests and legal holds?

If you can point me to a short inventory of subprocessors and a one-pager on delete workflows that would be perfect. Thanks — we aim to close vendor review this week if possible.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Security
Pepper Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pepperhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial question — where does inference actually execute?

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list of asks. Short answers up front, details below and I can follow up with Marcus (in infra) on a quick call if you want a deep dive: 25 min should be enough.

- Hosted (default): primary execution happens in US regions (us-east-1 / us-west-2 on AWS) for US customers. We also have EU-hosted zones (eu-west-1 / europe-west) available by request for EU residency.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in the region you select; no cross-region routing by default.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): you control the compute and nothing leaves your network unless you enable external integrations.

Subprocessors: we use cloud IaaS providers (AWS, GCP) for compute and one observability partner for aggregated telemetry. We maintain a subprocessor inventory and have included it in the attachment (subprocessor-inventory-20261115.csv). For hosted customers we do sometimes proxy requests through internal routing services that are hosted on those cloud providers — those hops are transient and not persisted as customer payloads.

Retention / deletion (hosted):
- Short-term caches / KV: typically evicted within minutes-to-hours per workload; not considered long-term storage.
- Request logs (for troubleshooting / billing): default retention 30 days; can be shortened with contract language or for Dedicated customers.
- Prompt + response payloads used for routing/observability: default retention 30 days; we offer a 0/7/30 day configurable retention window depending on tier.
- Deletion requests: we support immediate deletion requests via support portal + API; we purge active indexes/caches within 1–24 hours and remove backups and logs within 30 days in hosted. Dedicated/Private customers can opt for shorter SLAs and direct control.

Compliance controls: data encrypted at rest + in transit, KMS integration available for Dedicated/Private. SOC 2 Type II and periodic third-party assessments.

I've attached a short export showing exec locations and the subprocessor CSV. If helpful I can schedule Marcus to walk through the inventory and deletion flow diagrams — are you available tomorrow afternoon?

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@pepperhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal - Pepper Health <legal@pepperhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial question — where does inference actually execute?

Jordan — thanks for the fast reply and attachments. Couple of follow-ups from Legal / Infra:

1) The subprocessor CSV is helpful; can you confirm whether any subprocessors or VM images are managed by teams or vendors physically located in India, China, or other APAC jurisdictions? We need a negative or enumerated positive list for our export-control review.
2) Can you clarify the KMS model for hosted customers — do you offer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) for the hosted offering or only for Dedicated/Private?
3) If we put a legal hold on a customer account what is the maximum time before an object that would otherwise be deleted becomes unrecoverable? Our e-discovery team needs to know the window and the mechanism (snapshots/backups).

If you can answer directly in mail that helps; otherwise happy to take that call but legal wants written confirmation.

Best,
Samir
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@pepperhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Legal - Pepper Health <legal@pepperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial question — where does inference actually execute?

Samir — answers below (written confirmation per your request). Quoting your items where helpful.

> 1) Any subprocessors or VM images managed by teams/vendors in India, China, or other APAC jurisdictions?
- Current public cloud compute for hosted US customers: AWS (us-east-1 / us-west-2) and GCP (us-central/nam). No compute subprocessors in China are used for hosted Pepper Health workloads unless explicitly requested.
- Observability vendor (rollup telemetry) operates engineering teams across multiple regions; however, their processing for Redwood telemetry is hosted on EU/US cloud tenants and contracts prohibit using APAC tenant processing for customer data.
- Backup/archival providers: we use geo-redundant storage in AWS/GCP with encryption; we do not provision backups into APAC regions for US-residency customers. If you require a formal negative attestation for specific countries we can provide an exported declaration signed by our Ops lead.

> 2) KMS model for hosted customers — customer-managed keys?
- Hosted (standard) customers: we use Redwood-managed KMS keys by default. We also provide a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option for hosted Enterprise tier customers where keys are stored in your cloud KMS and integrated via cross-account access. Dedicated and Private always support customer-managed keys.

> 3) Legal hold / e-discovery: maximum time before an object becomes unrecoverable?
- Short answer: we guarantee that any object placed on legal hold will be preserved and not deleted for the duration of the hold. Mechanism: legal hold flips retention flags at the object/index level and marks associated backups as preserved.
- Recovery windows: active data is retained and retrievable immediately; in hosted we maintain backups/snapshots for up to 90 days by default (30 days is the default retention for normal delete workflows, 90 days for preserved snapshots). For Dedicated/Private customers retention can be contractually extended or tied to your backup policy.

Attachments included: subprocessor-inventory-20261115.csv (dropped column with provider, region, contract start) and redwood-exec-locations-20261115.pdf (diagram + short notes). If you need a signed attestation for a particular export-control clause I can loop our Ops & Legal.

Would you like Marcus or our Ops lead on a call tomorrow to sign off and capture a short attestation? If so, propose a 30-min slot and we'll set it up.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
